result:
I wrote the solution to `final.py`. Its search score is **88.7 on the last run and 90.3 on the run before** (same code; runs vary by about ±2%). The baseline is about 1.0. I used **12 of the 24 scorer calls** over about 14 minutes.

I followed the skill's default budget of about 15 minutes and stopped there, with 12 calls unspent. I couldn't measure on the unseen instances, so as a stand-in I checked the final pick on harness seeds I never tuned on: 51.6 ms for c8 against 45.8 ms for the final version.

| | search score |
|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 |
| first champion (c1) | 64.3 |
| final pick (c18) | 90.3, then 88.7 on the confirming run |

**Why it's faster.** It returns exactly the reference's pairs: it matched the reference on over 1,500 small edge-case inputs and on every harness and stress input.
- **Identical sets first:** records with the same word set are grouped once and all their pairs emitted directly. After that, sets of 1–3 words can never pair and are skipped.
- **Small sets:** for distinct sets of up to 8 words, an 80% match is only possible with a subset that has exactly one word fewer. These go in an index keyed by (word, size) and are checked with a cheap subset test.
- **Larger sets:** a set is only compared with sets sharing one of its first few rarest words (prefix filtering). Sets index fewer words than they look up, and entries too small to match are trimmed from the front of each index list.
- Each candidate pair is checked with the exact rule from the docstring.

**Approaches tried:**
- **Kept:** grouping identical sets (64.3 → 70.6), counting word frequencies with a plain loop instead of importing `Counter` (80.7), the small-set subset index (86.1), indexing only one word per small set (87.8), and the shorter index prefix for larger sets (90.3).
- **Dropped after harness measurements:**
  - ordering words by hash instead of frequency: 9× slower
  - subset matching by sums of word hashes: slower
  - counting frequencies on a sample: no gain
  - counting by sorting all words: 3× slower
  - several loop micro-tweaks: within noise
- **Lower on the scorer:** skipping sets made mostly of one-off words scored 77.0 (harness timings were mixed).
- **Rejected by the scorer** (calls 3 and 5 were wasted on these): importing from `_collections`, and importing `gc` to pause garbage collection.

**Candidate log** (scorer calls in order):

| call | candidate | score | kept or dropped, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | c1 | 64.3 | first champion |
| 2 | c3 | 70.6 | kept: groups identical sets |
| 3 | c6 | invalid | `_collections` import rejected |
| 4 | c8 | 80.7 | kept: plain-loop counting |
| 5 | c13 | invalid | `gc` import rejected |
| 6 | c12 | 78.4 | dropped: tie within noise |
| 7 | c14 | 80.7 | dropped: tie within noise |
| 8 | c15 | 77.0 | dropped: lower |

| 10 | c17 | 87.8 | kept: one indexed word per small set |

The test harness (`harness.py`, `bench.py`, `stress.py`, `phase.py`) and all the candidate files are left in the folder.
